lines.text: Here are four X tiles and four O tiles. There are seventy ways to line them up.
lines.caption: Here are four X tiles and four O tiles. There are seventy ways to line them up.

lines.text: But in only some of them, X never falls behind. <short pause> How many?
lines.caption: But in only some of them, X never falls behind. How many?

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find out, together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find out, together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Nora writes a string with the letter X four times, and the letter O four times.
lines.caption: Nora writes a string with the letter X four times, and the letter O four times.

lines.text: She reads it from left to right.
lines.caption: She reads it from left to right.

lines.text: At every point, the X count so far must be at least the O count so far.
lines.caption: At every point, the X count so far must be at least the O count so far.

lines.text: How many such strings are there?
lines.caption: How many such strings are there?

lines.text: Is it eight, fourteen, sixteen, twenty, or thirty-five?
lines.caption: Is it eight, fourteen, sixteen, twenty, or thirty-five?

lines.text: So what does that rule really mean?
lines.caption: So what does that rule really mean?

lines.text: Let's read a string and keep score, like a game between X and O.
lines.caption: Let's read a string and keep score, like a game between X and O.

lines.text: Look at this one. After every letter, the X count is at least the O count.
lines.caption: Look at this one. After every letter, the X count is at least the O count.

lines.text: Ties are fine. But X can never fall behind. So this one counts!
lines.caption: Ties are fine. But X can never fall behind. So this one counts!

lines.text: Now this one. After three letters, O leads, two to one. So it's out!
lines.caption: Now this one. After three letters, O leads, two to one. So it's out!

lines.text: Our job is to count every string where O never takes the lead.
lines.caption: Our job is to count every string where O never takes the lead.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Our first strategy is to make an organized list.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Our first strategy is to make an organized list.

lines.text: Two quick facts first. The first letter must be an X.
lines.caption: Two quick facts first. The first letter must be an X.

lines.text: If it were an O, then O would lead, one to zero.
lines.caption: If it were an O, then O would lead, one to zero.

lines.text: And the last letter must be an O.
lines.caption: And the last letter must be an O.

lines.text: If it were an X, then after seven letters, the O count would be four, and the X count only three. O would lead!
lines.caption: If it were an X, then after seven letters, the O count would be four, and the X count only three. O would lead!

lines.text: Now let's sort the strings by the X count before the first O.
lines.caption: Now let's sort the strings by the X count before the first O.

lines.text: All four X tiles first? Then the rest are O tiles. That's just one string.
lines.caption: All four X tiles first? Then the rest are O tiles. That's just one string.

lines.text: Three X tiles, then an O. The last X can go in three spots, but never at the very end. That's three strings.
lines.caption: Three X tiles, then an O. The last X can go in three spots, but never at the very end. That's three strings.

lines.text: Two X tiles, then an O. Let's list them carefully. We find five strings.
lines.caption: Two X tiles, then an O. Let's list them carefully. We find five strings.

lines.text: One X, then an O. That's a tie. Let's list the rest carefully. Five more strings.
lines.caption: One X, then an O. That's a tie. Let's list the rest carefully. Five more strings.

lines.text: One, plus three, plus five, plus five. <short pause> That's fourteen!
lines.caption: One, plus three, plus five, plus five. That's fourteen!

lines.text: Lists work well when they're short. But they grow fast!
lines.caption: Lists work well when they're short. But they grow fast!

lines.text: Here's a cleverer way. Let's turn each string into a walk.
lines.caption: Here's a cleverer way. Let's turn each string into a walk.

lines.text: Start at the top left corner. Each X steps right. Each O steps down.
lines.caption: Start at the top left corner. Each X steps right. Each O steps down.

lines.text: Here's our good string from before, drawn as a walk on the grid.
lines.caption: Here's our good string from before, drawn as a walk on the grid.

lines.text: The rule says the O count can never pass the X count. So the walk can never step below this wall.
lines.caption: The rule says the O count can never pass the X count. So the walk can never step below this wall.

lines.text: The string that failed goes below the wall, right here.
lines.caption: The string that failed goes below the wall, right here.

lines.text: Every good string is one walk to this corner. So let's count the walks!
lines.caption: Every good string is one walk to this corner. So let's count the walks!

lines.text: In each spot, we'll write how many walks can reach it.
lines.caption: In each spot, we'll write how many walks can reach it.

lines.text: Along the top, there's only one way: X after X. So we write ones.
lines.caption: Along the top, there's only one way: X after X. So we write ones.

lines.text: Any other spot is reached by a step from the left, or a step from above.
lines.caption: Any other spot is reached by a step from the left, or a step from above.

lines.text: So the number in a spot is the left number, plus the number above.
lines.caption: So the number in a spot is the left number, plus the number above.

lines.text: On the wall, the spot to the left is past the wall, so it doesn't count. We just copy the one above.
lines.caption: On the wall, the spot to the left is past the wall, so it doesn't count. We just copy the one above.

lines.text: Then one plus one is two. Two plus one is three. Three plus one is four.
lines.caption: Then one plus one is two. Two plus one is three. Three plus one is four.

lines.text: Next row. Copy the two. Two plus three is five. Five plus four is nine.
lines.caption: Next row. Copy the two. Two plus three is five. Five plus four is nine.

lines.text: Next, copy the five. Then five plus nine is fourteen.
lines.caption: Next, copy the five. Then five plus nine is fourteen.

lines.text: And the corner copies the fourteen. <short pause> Fourteen walks, so fourteen strings!
lines.caption: And the corner copies the fourteen. Fourteen walks, so fourteen strings!

lines.text: When would you pick the table? When a list would be too long. The table just adds!
lines.caption: When would you pick the table? When a list would be too long. The table just adds!

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Thirty-five is half of all seventy strings. But the good ones are NOT half.
lines.caption: Thirty-five is half of all seventy strings. But the good ones are NOT half.

lines.text: Next up, twenty. That counts every string that starts with X and ends with O. But it forgets to check the middle, like this one.
lines.caption: Next up, twenty. That counts every string that starts with X and ends with O. But it forgets to check the middle, like this one.

lines.text: Sixteen comes from guessing a pattern. Our groups went one, three, five, and then five again, not seven.
lines.caption: Sixteen comes from guessing a pattern. Our groups went one, three, five, and then five again, not seven.

lines.text: And eight is just too few. Our list found more.
lines.caption: And eight is just too few. Our list found more.

lines.text: So here's the habit. Count in a clear order, and check the rule at EVERY step.
lines.caption: So here's the habit. Count in a clear order, and check the rule at EVERY step.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Here's a twist.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Here's a twist.

lines.text: Now Nora uses the letter X five times, and the letter O only three times.
lines.caption: Now Nora uses the letter X five times, and the letter O only three times.

lines.text: At every point, the X count must still be at least the O count.
lines.caption: At every point, the X count must still be at least the O count.

lines.text: How many strings are there now? Use the table!
lines.caption: How many strings are there now? Use the table!

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. The walk now goes five steps right, and three steps down.
lines.caption: Let's check. The walk now goes five steps right, and three steps down.

lines.text: The first five columns are the same, and we stop one row sooner.
lines.caption: The first five columns are the same, and we stop one row sooner.

lines.text: We just add one new column. The top spot is one, as always.
lines.caption: We just add one new column. The top spot is one, as always.

lines.text: Then four plus one is five. Nine plus five is fourteen.
lines.caption: Then four plus one is five. Nine plus five is fourteen.

lines.text: And fourteen plus fourteen is <short pause> twenty-eight!
lines.caption: And fourteen plus fourteen is twenty-eight!

lines.text: If you found all twenty-eight strings, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found all twenty-eight strings, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Turn each string into a walk, and never cross the wall.
lines.caption: Turn each string into a walk, and never cross the wall.

lines.text: Then fill in a table. Each spot adds the ways in from the left, and from above.
lines.caption: Then fill in a table. Each spot adds the ways in from the left, and from above.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep counting, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep counting, and I'll see you next time!
